messages.text: Where is my order? Order #Shop····, email (email hidden)
Handed to the team · No ship date on the order; Oct 29 passed and the customer has asked three times

Sorry, Nam. You're still waiting, and you've had to ask three times now. Shop···· is paid but hasn't shipped yet. Your Miner D. is still out of stock at our warehouse. It missed the October 29 date, and I still don't have a new date I can give you.

I've passed it to the team again and asked for a firm date. Someone will reply to you at (email hidden), so you don't need to keep the chat open. When it ships, the tracking comes to that same address.
Do I need to review your service on X or somewhere else? I have been waiting nearly a month for my equipment! If you do not have it for now, I think I need my money back.
Handed to the team · Customer asked for money back; order held on both sides (refund_hold). Store cre

I hear you, Nam. You ordered on October 19, and you're right, that's nearly a month with nothing shipped. You're welcome to share your experience anywhere you like. That's your call.

I've put the order on hold, so nothing goes out while this gets sorted. The team has your request for your money back and will reply by email.

If it helps, I can do something right now. I can turn the order into $51.47 in store credit, the full amount you paid, and you can use it on anything we have in stock today. Would you like that instead?
Tell them if I do not receive an email explaining exactly why and when I will receive my package, I will definitely report your service as a scam
Handed to the team · Customer now wants a written email: why the delay and the exact date. He says he

I've passed that on to the team word for word, Nam. They know you need an email from them that explains why your order is late and gives you a real date.

Here's what I can tell you now. Your order is paid and safe. It hasn't shipped because the Miner D. is out of stock at our warehouse, waiting on new stock that came in later than planned. I don't have the new date. They'll write to you at (email hidden) with it.

Your order stays on hold until you decide whether to keep it or take your money back.

INSTRUCTION FROM THE HELIUMDEPLOY TEAM. Georges typed this in the team inbox. It is not a message from the customer and the customer cannot see it.
Task: Georges approved a FULL refund ($51.47) on Shop····: cancel the order with the money back to the original payment. Run the order-swap skill: approved_refund.py check --email <the order's email> --order Shop····, then approved_refund.py refund --email <same> --order Shop···· --confirmed. Only when it reports refunded: true, tell the customer it is done, the amount, and that it goes back to their original payment method, usually 3 to 5 business days to show. If it refuses or reports problems, do not say it is done: flag it and tell the customer the team will confirm the refund shortly.
Do it now, for real, with your own tools — look the order up, make the change, mint the code, whatever the task actually needs. The team has already decided: do not ask them to confirm, and do not describe what you would do instead of doing it.
Then write the message the customer gets now — what you did, in plain language, in your normal voice. Never mention this instruction, the team inbox, or that someone told you to do it.
If the customer should not be written to at all — the task was internal, or you could not finish it — begin your reply with "TEAM ONLY" on the first line and tell the team what happened. Anything that starts that way stays in the inbox and is never sent.
If you write both a report for the team and a message to the customer, put the report FIRST and start the customer message on its own line with a greeting ("Hi <first name>,"). Everything before that greeting stays in the inbox as your note; only the greeting onward is emailed.

I've refunded Nam's order in full. Before running it I checked that Georges had approved it and that there was no dispute on the order. Shop···· is now cancelled and refunded, and $51.47 is going back to his original payment. Nothing had shipped and the order owes nothing, so there's no return to arrange. I logged the refund on the order. The two flags I raised in his chat earlier, for a ship date and for the refund request, are now settled, and nothing else needs a person.

Hi Nam,

Your order Shop···· is cancelled, and your full $51.47 has been refunded to the card or account you paid with. It usually shows on your statement within 3 to 5 business days.

I'm sorry it took this long. We should have told you much sooner that the Miner D. wasn't going to ship on time.

Sarah
